text: When the gods and the demons churned the ocean of milk, the first thing it gave up was poison.
Halahala: dark enough to end every world.
asr: Hala Hala, dark enough to end every world.

text: Shiva took it in his hands, and drank it. He held it in his throat, and his throat turned blue.
So he is called Neelakantha, the blue-throated one: the destroyer who saved the world from destruction.
asr: So he is called Nila Kanta, the blue-throated one. The destroyer who saved the world from destruction.

text: He is the ascetic of Mount Kailash, the first of all yogis, and the dancer whose steps undo the world, so that it can begin again.
asr: He is the ascetic of Mount Kailash, the first of all yogas, and the dancer who steps undo the world so that it can begin again.

text: In the south of India, five great temples honour him as the five elements of which everything is made.
asr: In the south of India, five great temples honor him as the five elements of which everything is made.

text: Earth, at Kanchipuram, where he is worshipped in a lingam of sand, beneath an ancient mango tree.
asr: Earth at Kanchapuram, where he has worshipped in a lingam of sand beneath an ancient mango tree.

text: Water, at Thiruvanaikaval, where a spring rises in the sanctum, and the shrine is never fully dry.
asr: water at Thiruvannakaval, where a spring rises in the sanctum and the shrine is never fully dry.

text: Fire, at Tiruvannamalai. Each year, at the festival of Karthigai, a great flame is lit on the summit of the hill.
asr: Fire at Taru Van Amalai. Each year at the Festival of Karthagai, a great flame is lit on the summit of the hill.

text: Air, at Srikalahasti, where a lamp in the inner shrine is said to flicker, though no wind can reach it.
asr: air at Srikkel-A-Hasty, where a lamp in the inner shrine is said to flicker, though no wind can reach it.

text: And space, at Chidambaram, where he dances as Nataraja.
Behind a curtain there, the secret of Chidambaram is revealed: an empty space. Nothing to see, because the formless has no form.
asr: Behind a curtain there, the secret of Chit Embaram is revealed. An empty space. Nothing to see because the formless has no form.

text: His mantra has five syllables, one for each element.
Nah.
Mah.
Shee.
Vah.
Yah.
Aum. Namah Shivaya.
The world is painted, kept, and washed away. And the paper beneath it was always there.
